Found facts and right answers

1. Agentic GraphRAG mostly finds some of the facts, not all of them

Comparison: it finds no gold facts on 8 to 12 questions per repeat, against 19 for Normal RAG, but all of them on 16 to 20, against 20. Temporal: no facts on 9 to 13 against 13, all facts on 15 to 19 against 15.

With all gold facts found, both methods get 73 to 93% of those questions right. With only some found, 42 to 54%.

2. "Insufficient information" usually means a missing article

When Normal RAG or Agentic GraphRAG replies "Insufficient information" to a comparison or temporal question, at least one article the question needs was not retrieved in 94 to 100% of cases. Only 0 to 3 of these replies per repeat came with all gold facts found.

3. On temporal questions, guessing pays

Most temporal answers are Yes or No. HippoRAG replies "Insufficient information" to 32 or 33 of them per repeat, Normal RAG to 44 to 48. Of the 24 temporal questions where HippoRAG finds no gold facts, it still gets 10 to 12 right.

1. The question

Do knowledge graphs make multi-hop RAG better? We compare Normal RAG, RAPTOR, HippoRAG and Agentic GraphRAG one question type at a time.

2. What we found

On comparison and inference questions, Normal RAG is as accurate as the graph methods. Graphs help on temporal questions: HippoRAG gets 59 to 60 of 100 right and Agentic GraphRAG 54 to 58, against 47 to 51 for Normal RAG. On comparison and temporal questions, most wrong answers come with an article missing from the retrieved text.

3. What we have

400 questions no method was tuned on, 3 repeats, the same answer model and prompt for every method, and the check of found facts against right answers on slide 6.

4. Still needed

Rerun HotpotQA with 3 repeats. Build and test a way to spot temporal questions for the router. Add one more dataset. Have a judge check the refusals.

GPT-6-LUNA GOLD-FACT JUDGE, STEP 1: split each gold sentence into claims, the gold facts

Answered right: the answer matches a gold answer after lowercasing and removing punctuation and a, an, the. If not, the Claude Haiku judge on the left decides whether it names the same entity, value or yes or no. An "Insufficient information" reply that does not match counts as wrong. Gold facts found: the gpt-6-luna judge on the right splits each gold sentence into claims, then checks each claim against the retrieved text. A claim counts as found only when the judge marks it stated and its quote appears in the retrieved text.

Comparison questions compare two articles or entities. The same 100 in every repeat, out of 856 in the dataset.
Temporal questions ask about the order of events or whether two dates agree. The same 100 in every repeat, out of 583 in the dataset.
Inference questions name an entity by combining facts. The same 100 in every repeat, out of 816 in the dataset.
Null questions cite articles that are not in the collection, so the only right reply is "Insufficient information". The same 100 in every repeat, out of 301 in the dataset.
